name: Kou
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page sins1241 (Kou); Glottolog hh.bib entries tagged [snz]
sources.note: Zero descriptive references; only overview/wordlist items (Claassen & McElhanon 1970, Z'graggen 1975, 1980, O'Bannon et al. 2022, two anonymous 'Ramu Wordlists' manuscripts of 9 pp. held in the Glottolog/hh archive, not online).

sources.citation: O'Bannon, Devin, Mary O'Bannon, North Cady & April Hope. 2022. Kou Survey Report: A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Kou/Sensauru [snz] Language of Madang Province. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-017. Dallas: SIL International. 59 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (EGIDS, dialect mapping); Appendix E (pp. 40-52) gives IPA 120-item wordlists for 8 villages with no stress marks; sec. 2.1.5 (p. 8) says only that lists 'were transcribed using the International Phonetic Alphabet'. Sec. 1.2 (pp. 2-3) inventories all earlier work: unpublished SIL wordlists only.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Change Request 2018-012: merge [asd] Asas into [snz], rename to Kou (adopted 2019-01-25). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; naming/identity only (Asas and Sinsauru are one language called Kou, Sensauru used further from the highway).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction sec. 7 (pp. vii-ix): 'The transcription of the word list is rendered in a semiphonemic form, i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; lists consonant fluctuations for Sinsauru (f~h, r~l) and Asas (f~p, p~h); no stress marks in the B1 Sinsauru / B2 Asas columns.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. vi+154 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification, village and population lists (B1 Sinsauru, B2 Asas 'Kow'); no phonology.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification and lexicostatistics; sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.1 defines the Evapia family (Sinsauru, Asas, Sausi, Kesawai, Dumpu) and sorts out the Koropa/Kaikovu wordlist confusions; no phonology.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 6.1.3 (p. 64) on the Evapia family: voiceless stops, contrastive voiced stops in 'Koropa and Sinsauru', nasals labial/alveolar, vibrant, lateral, continuants [f s h w y], five vowels i e a o u. Segmental only; the two 'stress' hits in the volume belong to Bunn & Bunn's Golin paper.

sources.citation: Onken, Mark (consultant); Kibu, T., F. Korae, M. Yago, A. Lobua, Y. Kibu & T. Manano. 2000. Kou Saul: Trial Spelling Guide for the Kou Language (189-word dictionary, stories, songs). Sausi Station: SIL PNG. 16 pp.

sources.citation: Priestley, Carol & Malcolm Ross. 1979. Kou/Sinsauru data (wordlists and texts, 'new Saipa at Monopeya River'). Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG. Ms.

sources.note: The only recorded texts of the language, taken by two linguists (Ross); a field transcription with texts is the item most likely to carry stress marks or a prosodic note. Cited in O'Bannon et al. 2022 sec. 1.2.
